entities.summary:
Jöns Budde, OSsS, was a Bridgettine monk from the Bridgettine convent Vallis gratiae, the first convent for women in Finland, located in Naantali, near Turku, Finland – at the time part of the Kalmar Union (1397–1523).

Born in 1435, Budde played a pivotal role in the establishment of the convent, which was consecrated in 1463. He was also involved in the translation of several Latin texts into Finnish, contributing to the development of the Finnish language.

The convent's significance extends beyond its role in Finnish history, as it marks the beginning of a tradition of female religious education in Finland. Budde's work also highlights the importance of the Kalmar Union, which united Sweden, Norway, and Denmark under a single monarch from 1397 to 1523.

The legacy of Vallis gratiae can be seen in the modern-day Finnish Catholic Church, which continues to venerate Budde as a saint. His contributions to Finnish language and culture have had a lasting impact, making him an important figure in Finnish history.

Budde's story serves as a testament to the power of faith and education in shaping the course of human history. His work continues to inspire generations of scholars and linguists, ensuring his place in the annals of world history.

The fact that Budde was the first monk to be ordained in Finland, at the age of 26, underscores the significance of his role in establishing a new religious order in the region.
